chosen.premise: Goldeen are admired for their fins, yet they compete with one another to grow the thickest and sharpest horn.
chosen.hook: Goldeen has a beauty contest—but the prize is the best horn.
chosen.visualIdea: Show elegant Goldeen posing, then turn it into a scoreboard ranking horns by thickness and sharpness.
chosen.note: The strangest and most character-specific premise: Goldeen apparently compete over horn thickness and sharpness. “Beauty contest” and “prize” are creative framing rather than explicit research facts.

candidates.premise: Goldeen looks like a water queen, but one horn ram can shatter even the thickest aquarium glass.
candidates.hook: This elegant fish can smash its way out of an aquarium.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Goldeen gliding like a dancer, then cut to its horn cracking a thick glass tank.
candidates.note: A highly Goldeen-specific contradiction: elegant fins versus aquarium-shattering horn. The glass claim is directly supported, though “one horn ram” slightly compresses the wording.

candidates.premise: Goldeen’s dress-like fins project royalty, but its sharp horn is powerful enough to strike back when danger appears.
candidates.hook: Goldeen’s royal outfit hides a weapon.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen the flowing tail fin against a sudden close-up of Goldeen jabbing with its horn.
candidates.note: Clearly captures Goldeen’s elegance-versus-danger contradiction and is easy to stage visually, but it overlaps substantially with the stronger aquarium-smashing angle.

candidates.premise: Goldeen can swim nonstop up fast streams at five knots, turning an elegant fish into a relentless river climber.
candidates.hook: Goldeen can swim upstream nonstop at five knots.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate a five-knot speed gauge as Goldeen pushes continuously against rushing water.
candidates.note: The precise five-knot speed and nonstop upstream swimming are strongly supported, but the basic “strong swimmer” framing is less distinctive than Goldeen’s other contradictions.

candidates.premise: When spring arrives, schools of Goldeen form groups and swim upriver and up waterfalls to lay eggs.
candidates.hook: Every spring, Goldeen turns rivers into a migration highway.
candidates.visualIdea: Reveal a lone Goldeen, then widen to a huge school surging up a river and waterfall.
candidates.note: Well-supported and visually expansive, combining spawning, schools, upriver travel, and waterfalls. It is compelling but resembles real fish-migration stories and is less sharply surprising.

candidates.premise: Goldeen remains a Water-type queen until level 33, when it evolves into the also-Water-type Seaking.
candidates.hook: At level 33, Goldeen’s royal era ends.
candidates.visualIdea: Count up to level 33 as Goldeen’s silhouette flashes and resolves into Seaking, with Water unchanged.
candidates.note: The level-33 evolution and unchanged Water type are concrete, but the royal-era interpretation is subjective and the evolution fact is less inherently surprising.

rounds.request: If this angle were rejected, a stronger replacement would need an equally specific and unusual behavioral rule, with direct Pokédex support and a visual contrast that is unmistakably Goldeen-specific.
